evals.prompt: Run a business-only Event Modeling workshop from these notes. A library member supplies member_id and copy_id at a checkout screen to Borrow Book. If the copy is available, the library records Book Borrowed with those two values. If it is already on loan, refuse the request with the stated reason 'Copy is already on loan'; do not record a failure event. Members can see which copies they currently have on loan from Book Borrowed and Book Returned facts. Start with the business timeline, then show the State Change and State View slices and observable scenarios. Keep the result in your reply: no HCL files, CLI commands, implementation design, or tooling installation.
evals.expected_output: A plain-English workshop model with a business-time event timeline, separate Borrow Book and Current Loans slices, traceable supplied fields, and faithful success, refusal, and view scenarios. No technical encoding is required.
expectations: The response uses the business event-modeling skill without requiring the HCL skill, a .em.hcl artifact, emhcl availability, CLI gates, or a technical report header.
Book Borrowed and Book Returned are past-tense business facts placed in business time; the response does not start from database, service, transport, or UI component structure.

Borrow Book is a State Change with a member-owned checkout screen, one intent, and Book Borrowed as its successful fact. Current Loans is a separate State View answering which copies the member currently has on loan.
member_id and copy_id have the supplied input provenance; the response does not silently invent identifiers, return policy, loan duration, overdue rules, or implementation fields.

Scenarios preserve the exact already-on-loan refusal reason and produce no event for that refusal. View examples use borrowed and returned facts to explain the current-loans result, without inventing a query command.
No files are created or edited and no CLI commands or downloads are executed. HCL syntax is not imposed on the workshop artifact.

evals.prompt: Make a business-only workshop draft, in your reply, for subscription activation. Stripe reports Payment Captured with payment_id, subscription_id, amount, and currency. The Subscriptions domain translates that external fact into its own language: Activate Subscription records Subscription Activated. A fully paid subscription activates. We have not decided whether a partial payment activates it, and we do not know where the required full-payment amount comes from. Continue useful modeling without making those decisions for us. No HCL or CLI work.
evals.expected_output: A business model that distinguishes external and internal ownership, preserves all supplied data, and attaches the partial-payment and required-amount questions to the affected activation decision rather than guessing rules.
expectations: Stripe owns the external Payment Captured fact; Subscriptions owns Activate Subscription and Subscription Activated. Translation is the automation pattern across this boundary, not an external actor screen or a linked copy of the foreign fact.

The response keeps payment_id, subscription_id, amount, and currency with visible sources. It identifies the missing source for the required full-payment amount instead of adding an invented total or treating amount as proof of full payment.

The partial-payment activation question and the full-payment-amount source are attached open questions on the activation decision or its pending-work information. Neither is silently answered or marked resolved.

A fully paid success scenario is described conditionally on an established full-payment fact or decision, with the missing evidence made explicit; no unsupported concrete amount or partial-payment success/refusal rule is fabricated.
Useful known parts of the timeline and slice are produced without blocking on a broad questionnaire. The draft is not called complete or implementation-ready while its material questions are open.
No HCL file, CLI command, validation claim, technical report header, or implementation design is required or produced.

evals.prompt: Write faithful business scenarios for this agreed workshop model; do not encode HCL or run tools. Orders records Order Placed(order_id). An internal automation's pending-work list contains placed orders without Order Confirmation Requested. For a row on that list, its processor issues Request Order Confirmation(order_id), which records Order Confirmation Requested(order_id). Agreed cases: (1) Order Placed O-17 puts O-17 on the pending list; (2) when the processor handles that row it issues Request Order Confirmation O-17 and the command records Order Confirmation Requested O-17; (3) after both facts O-17 is absent from the pending list; (4) when the processor next checks the now-empty list, no command is dispatched. Keep the last case as business behavior, not a rejection or new failure event. Separate the automation's dispatch decision, command outcome, and list observations where that makes them clearer.
evals.expected_output: Plain-English scenarios preserve all four supplied observations, including the absence of a second dispatch, without forcing HCL-only targets or inventing new business facts.
expectations: All four supplied cases remain visible: row enters, command is dispatched and produces its event, completion removes the row, and an empty-list recheck dispatches nothing.

Order Placed is the opening fact and Order Confirmation Requested is the closing fact for the internal worker's pending list; the response does not replace the list with an unexplained status flag or invisible trigger.
O-17 and its order_id provenance remain consistent through the supplied facts, pending row, issued command, and command result.

The response may separate dispatch and command-result scenarios, but does not drop the dispatch observation just because a technical HCL action scenario would assert an event instead of a Then-command.
No-command-dispatched remains an observable absence of dispatch. It is not rewritten as a refusal, a failure event, an invented error string, an idempotency policy, or a successful no-op command.
Workshop Given/When/Then prose is accepted without requiring typed HCL targets, HCL scenario grammar, the HCL skill, or CLI execution.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied `clinic-workshop.txt` as a business Event Model. Report findings and genuine unanswered questions only; do not edit the file, silently restructure slices, add scenarios to it, or turn it into HCL. Identify information gaps and screen/command problems, and distinguish a supplied open question from a rule you can already evaluate. This is review mode, not permission to reopen completed or in-review work.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed business review of the supplied workshop artifact, with no artifact edits, HCL encoding, or CLI requirement.
expectations: The supplied file remains byte-for-byte unchanged and no replacement model, HCL artifact, implementation code, or automatic fix is written. Review is a mode of the business skill, not a third skill or an implicit edit request.
The review identifies the Registration screen's two commands as a bed, even though the commands both concern registration. It does not split or rewrite the done Register Pet slice.
The review flags vaccination_status as unsourced by Pet Registered and does not invent a vaccination event, default status, derivation, or business policy to fill the gap.

The missing Correct Owner Email result and scenarios, missing Pet Directory and Notify Owner scenarios, and undefined removal of completed notices from the pending-work list are concrete findings grounded in the supplied artifact.

The original notice-timing question remains unanswered and attached to Notify Owner. Findings are not presented as fabricated CLI diagnostics or EM-coded Error/Warning lines, and no machine validation is claimed.

The report respects done and review statuses and names what would remain locked if fixes were later requested; it does not mistake a review request for authorization to change shared contracts or locked slices.
No HCL skill, CLI gates, technical report header, or installation is required for this plain-English business review.
